title: Claim: alleged hacker says they are selling a Balanz client database
date_note: La Política Online's publication day; the page gives no earlier day for the claim.
place: Argentina (Balanz is an Argentine financial firm per the article; no city given)
geo_basis: country as stated by the source (Argentine firm); Buenos Aires used as the pin for the country, no city given
summary: La Política Online reports that an alleged hacker says they have a database of 2,55 millones de registros of Balanz clients for sale, with names, national ID numbers, tax IDs, phones, emails and addresses. The outlet says there is no independent check that the files are authentic or that an intrusion into the company’s systems occurred. It also says Balanz gave no known official response.
plain: An unnamed person claims to be selling client data from the Argentine firm Balanz. Nobody has verified the files, and Balanz has not responded publicly, according to La Política Online.
exec: Unverified claim of a client-data sale involving Balanz; no confirmation from the company.
impact: Unconfirmed; the article says the figure is doubted and the files have not been independently verified.

evidence.quote: Un presunto hacker asegura tener a la venta una base con 2,55 millones de registros de clientes.
Sin embargo, hasta el momento no hay una comprobación independiente de que los archivos sean auténticos ni de que se haya producido una intrusión en los sistemas de la compañía.

validation.note: Single publisher (La Política Online) relaying an unnamed alleged hacker's claim; the article says there is no independent check and no known official Balanz response. No Balanz statement or regulator page was found.

report.note: La Política Online article read in full.

review.note: stronger than the source: removed data-breach tag from an unverified claim (article says no check of files or of an intrusion); summary now says so; evidence quote completed to the full sentence. Figure, date, status, severity checked against La Politica Online.
